verdicts.notes:
All 12 r2 cards checked against the live 4.3 pages, which all returned 200: implementation/log, implementation/message-format, configuration/topic-configs, design/design, getting-started/upgrade, plus the 4.3.1 javadoc for ProducerRecord and Admin. Every answer is correct. Balance is 6 true and 6 false, with average statement length 71.2 for true and 70.0 for false.

Cards that pass, with their evidence:
- 01: message-format calls RecordBatch the "on-disk format", and compressed record data is serialized inside it. design/design is more direct: "The batch will remain compressed in the log". The card is true only under the default topic compression.type=producer, which the default-context rule covers.
- 03: "the largest timestamp in a segment file ... defining the retention time for the entire segment".
- 04: "Since this limit is enforced at the partition level, multiply it by the number of partitions".
- 05: "Size-based retention is disabled by default". The explanation ("enables a ... limit when configured") adds almost nothing. A better one: retention.bytes defaults to -1, so only retention.ms removes segments unless a size limit is set.
- 06: segment.ms "force the log to roll even if the segment file isn't full".
- 07: "The \"delete\" policy (which is the default)".
- 09: the 4.2.0 notable changes say "cleanup.policy now supports empty values, which means infinite retention". The same notes add that deleteRecords can still remove segments, and that with remote storage local retention still applies. - 11: "written to a persistent log on the filesystem without necessarily flushing to disk" and "we do not want to require the use of fsync on every write".

Per-record tracking holds in both modes. Design page: 'Records are acknowledged individually ... Delivery attempts to consumers in a share group are counted', 'partitions may be assigned to multiple consumers', 'time-limited acquisition lock' and 'A share consumer holding the lock can handle the record in the following ways: Acknowledge ... Release ... Reject'. I added 'can' because Renew also exists. Keep appliesTo 'Kafka 4.2 and later' and volatility may_change. Statement 87 chars.

The statement is now 85 chars against the editor's 94, so this true card gets shorter and the r10 gap shrinks further. KafkaConsumer javadoc (4.3.1): 'markers are not returned to applications, yet have an offset in the log. As a result, applications reading from topics with transactional messages will see gaps in the consumed offsets ... filtered out for consumers in both isolation levels.'
